head_record.january_head_note: january's climbed head carries no published RMSE to gate against, so it is gated on the CLEAN board instead: its clean v12 is checked to sit within GATE of the published clean v12 board through board(clean12) above, and its all-row RMSE is recorded here rather than asserted.
head_record.rule: np.where(airport in exp-036 keep, head, v7), then + s*(stack-5 - it)

note:
, and what each fold's head is fitted on.**  `r11` exists only on the
three fold panels -- each panel is one validation month with an out-of-fold v11 -- so a
"fit on the 2025 months other than the scored fold" needs the block on those months.
The harvest delivered 2025-01 at 15:5x UTC on 2026-09-08, so ALL THREE folds now
rotate and the assignment's "every fold interval clear of zero" clause is evaluated on
three folds of three.  The panels are not the same size, and the record has to say so
(FALLBACK round 3, C3): **july_loo and december are each scored by a head fitted on ONE
panel** (december and july_loo respectively), **january by a head fitted on TWO**, and
the SERVED head in `code/serve.py` is fitted on all three.  So the fold table is a
lower bound on the served head's data, not a like-for-like reading of it.

projection_weights.note: per airport-MONTH (desk 17:05 UTC) and per REACH CLASS (FALLBACK round 3, blocking 1): the ranking block gives the rows, the class and the reached share, so an airport dark in one month (LIRF in 2026-07, LTFM in both) carries all of that month's rows in the no-clock class, none in the with-clock class, and almost all of them in the UNREACHED half, which is priced on the fold's own unreached rows.
